before_v8.abstract_text: Risk limits on dealer positions concern the largest magnitude reached before a review horizon ends, rather than the position at its endpoint. We compare historical and conditional quantile forecasts of sampled absolute-position peaks for an FX market maker and weekly primary-dealer position aggregates. Simple historical rules prove difficult to beat. At the shorter horizon, long-history FX regression lowers matched loss by 14.8% and 16.6% in the previously reported later and earlier windows. Its later advantage survives a delayed adaptive coverage adjustment (ACI). Before correction, however, regression breaches more frequently, while its ranking against a shorter-history rolling rule changes across periods. After stronger regularization, regression still loses 34 of 48 additional-panel comparisons. We formalize the known-floor target and apply a classical endpoint-to-peak bound under explicit assumptions. The results support joint validation of accuracy, breach behavior, and stability across reference rules, periods, and related series. A controlled simulation rejects a universal narrow-regime explanation, while aggregation and the overlapping backcast further qualify the empirical pattern.
